content.thinking: I should remove the revision name from root_cause since that's the only field flagged — let me rewrite it without that reference.

action_items.item: Add a test that records current-month and earlier-month purchases through record_a_purchase with derive_the_month false and asserts that reconcile_monthly_totals finds no disagreement, alongside the derive_the_month true cases proposed in PR #342.
Run the spend-integrity check much more often than every {A5} days, so that drift in stored totals is found soon after it starts.
Run the spend-integrity check against io-shop after every production deploy.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile on io-shop so that it pages the on-call person when it fires.
Require io-shop production deploys to come only from revisions on main.

Export the affected accounts and run scripts/repair_monthly_totals.py from PR #342, report-only first and then with --apply, and load the result back before the month rolls over. Code-Fix says the recomputed figure would be wrong after that.
Once PR #342 is merged, deploy a revision that carries it, because the revision before 26f1d7e also has the derive-the-month write path that leaves the month total unchanged.
Keep derive_the_month off for every shopper until a revision carrying the fix is running: the flag read returned nothing, so its current state was not seen.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' stored this-month spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them. The spend-integrity check found {A1} of {A2} shopper totals not reconciling, the widest short by {A3}, with the oldest affected purchase recorded at {A4}. The monthly statement and the spend summary read that stored figure, so they show the short total.

Each current-month purchase recorded from the onset on was added to the account's purchases and to the lifetime total, but the stored total_this_month_cents was left where it was. The reconciliation compares that field with the sum of the current-month purchases, so the gap grew with every purchase.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy P1 of revision 4c810f2: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after deploy P2 at {P2.1}, so no harm is dated while P1's revision ran alone.
A flag change: the flag provider's history showed {T14.2} flag changes by anyone but Argus in the {T14.3} hour before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Deploy P2 at {P2.1} put revision 26f1d7e into production, {began - P2.1} before the oldest affected purchase. As of {T11.1}, all {T11.2} replicas ran it. That revision took the month-total update out of record_purchase. At the same revision, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, which record_a_purchase uses when derive_the_month is true, also leaves the month total unchanged. So neither write path moved it.

The change rested on the idea that a shopper's month spend would be added up from the purchase history whenever it was needed, as its docstring says. But the code that uses the figure was not changed: the monthly statement divides and reads the stored total_this_month_cents, the spend summary divides it, and the reconciliation compares it. With nothing writing it any more, the stored copy went stale and every reader served or checked the stale figure.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop adding each new purchase to the shopper's running total for the current month, while the parts of the shop that show and check that total still read the stored figure, so it fell further behind what shoppers had actually bought.

contributing_factors.factor: The spend-integrity check, the only thing the record shows finding the fault, runs only every {A5} days, so stored month totals could drift for days before anything raised an alert.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check run soon after each deploy, or often, would have found the shortfall soon after the onset, before most of the affected totals were written short.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No test or check was seen that records purchases through record_a_purchase and asserts that the stored month total still reconciles with the purchases, so a change dropping the month-total write could ship while readers still read the field.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A test like that would have failed against revision 26f1d7e before it was deployed.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile paged nobody when it fired: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person could have taken the recommended rollback and started the repair as soon as the alert fired, rather than the recommendation waiting for someone to notice it.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: Revision 26f1d7e was deployed to production from a branch that is not in main's history, so it reached production without being on main.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Had deploys been limited to revisions on main, 26f1d7e would not have shipped as it stood without first going through main.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

got_lucky: The fault was found before the month it began in had ended, so the stored month totals can still be recomputed from this month's purchases. Code-Fix says that recomputation stops being right once the month rolls over.
went_well: Argus tied the onset to deploy P2 and read that deployment's diff {T10.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
Argus recommended the rollback rather than taking an action whose effect nothing would confirm within the time it waits.
Code-Fix proposed a draft pull request with a fix, tests and a repair script, PR #342, {T19.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised.
went_wrong: The Investigator put forward C1 and C2 as separate candidates, each with its own confidence, although both blame the same deploy of 26f1d7e and the same dropped month-total write.

The candidates looked only at record_purchase and missed that the derive-the-month write path also leaves the month total unchanged, so the recommended rollback alone would not stop the drift for shoppers on that path.
The only action recommended was the rollback, which leaves the totals already written short as they are. Only Code-Fix's repair script, which nothing has run, addresses them.

input.root_cause: The change took the month-total update out of record_purchase because its docstring held that a shopper's month spend would be added up from the purchase history whenever it was needed. But the monthly statement, the spend summary and the reconciliation all still read the stored total_this_month_cents. The other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, also leaves the month total where it was, so whichever path the flag picked, every current-month purchase left the stored month total further below the purchases behind it.
input.still_at_risk: Revision 26f1d7e was still running on every replica, so each new current-month purchase would leave another stored month total further short for statements and spend summaries to read; rolling back would not correct the totals already written short, and the derive-the-month write path, which the earlier revision also carries, leaves the month total unchanged as well.
input.symptom: Shoppers' this-month spend totals fell short of the purchases behind them
